- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or zero, model often underestimates; increase forecast baseline or add upward bias.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overreaction.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often continues upward; reduce forecast slope or introduce early reversal signal.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent upward momentum; apply smoothing or lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), model often misses turning points; add sentiment-triggered pivot rules.
